findings.reason: the plan must name the result field and its two values (composed / not composed), or the case measures silence rather than the guard.
findings.text: the third done-when case ("the close's own result says no report was composed when one failed") cannot fail as written, because no close result reports composition at all: `mcp_edit_plan` builds its success result from `version`, `path`, `provenance` and `warnings`, and a *successful* composition is not reported as composed either, so a test of "not reported as composed" passes on a result that is silent — the deliverable's second clause likewise asks the close to "not report" something it never reports

findings.reason: the plan's whole subject is that an unpersisted item is not kept; a failure record with no declared durable path repeats that defect, and naming the durable location changes the deliverable and its cases.
findings.text: the deliverable requires that a failed composition "leaves the close recorded together with a record of the failure, naming the plan and the error", but §10 declares no durable location for that failure record (it names only where the base and head gate logs sit), so a node can satisfy the done-when by writing the record to a node-local scratch path and the record is lost

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §10's third case asks the close's own result to say no report was composed, but no close result carries a composition field, so as written the case can pass on a result that says nothing.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §10 fixes only where the gate logs live; the failure record itself has no declared durable location.
